one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of how much of a retrieved-experience bank's benefit survives once a reflective prompt optimizer is given the identical training episodes - the substitution ratio S = 1 - (gain at I1)/(gain at I0) - together with a compile-the-whole-bank-once instruction arm (C) token-matched against live top-k retrieval, a co-adaptation cell (I2), and a non-compilable positive-control bank (B-dup) that certifies the instrument can still detect non-substitutable value.
closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (cited as arXiv 2607.05202) is the direct threat: it already places Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on the same 528/267 train/test trajectories across four domains and three backbones, and its reported headline - ReasoningBank about +7 on Qwen backbones, GEPA nearly matching a curated reference on Gemma-4-31B, no automatic method positive in every cell - is qualitatively the proposal's thesis. What survives is genuinely marginal-but-real: the combined I1xM1 and I2xM1/I2xM0 cells, token matching, the compiled arm, instance-paired McNemar/TOST, and the positive control. The problem is that a reader who has EvoAgentBench already believes 'an optimized instruction gets you most of what a bank gets you'; this proposal converts a believed qualitative claim into a number with error bars, which is a solid workshop-to-borderline-main-track contribution, not a new claim. The second threat is Experience Distillation (2607.21051): its 'retains >=64.8% of the in-context gain' is literally S with weights as the second container, so the metric shape is not new either - only the choice of container is. Note that the entire novelty argument rests on an unverified negative claim about EvoAgentBench's contents (no combined cell, no token matching, no paired statistics), which is exactly the kind of appendix-level detail that web-search snippets cannot establish.
strongest_objection: S cannot separate substitution from saturation. S is a difference-in-differences of raw accuracy across two prompts sitting at different baseline levels: cells 5/6 (I1xM0, I1xM1) versus 1/2 (I0xM0, I0xM1). If GEPA works at all - and gate G2 requires it to, at >=2pt on 3 of 4 seeds - then I1xM0 is above I0xM0, so the pool of items memory can still fix has shrunk before memory is ever injected. On a bounded 0-1 scale the memory gain then compresses mechanically, H2's TOST at +/-4pt passes, and Prediction 1 (S >= 0.6, CI excluding 0.3) is satisfied with zero information having been transferred between containers. Nothing in the design distinguishes 'the optimizer absorbed the bank's content' from 'there was less left to fix'; the fix/break decomposition diagnoses churn but is not a control for headroom, and I3 controls for length, not for level. This compounds with a selection problem in the denominator: A1 was chosen because a prior study measured +7.7pt on it, and G1 then re-selects on the same quantity at n=150, where by the proposal's own MDE arithmetic (3.5pt at n=1000) the detectable effect is roughly 9pt - a 6pt gate at that n can be passed by a true effect near 2pt. Both selection on the prior estimate and selection on the gate bias the S denominator upward, and S is inflated by exactly that bias. A reviewer can therefore accept every number in the paper and reject the conclusion.
what_would_fix_it: Three concrete changes. (1) Add an accuracy-matched, information-disjoint instruction control: run GEPA on a disjoint training set S_train2 that shares no episodes with the bank (or titrate a hand-written instruction to I1's accuracy), then measure the memory gain at that instruction. If the gain collapses there too, the collapse is headroom, not substitution; if it survives, S measures what the title says. This single arm is worth more than the MIPROv2 generality check, the LoRA arm and the iso-cost curve combined and should be promoted above them in the contingency order. (2) Define S on the logit/odds-ratio scale using the crossed-random-effects model already specified, and additionally report memory's gain restricted to the items I1xM0 still gets wrong (a conditional-on-remaining-errors version of S); report both alongside the raw-accuracy S. (3) Estimate the denominator from the fresh S_test I0 cells with an explicitly shrunken/selection-corrected prior rather than treating +7.7pt as the expected value, and pre-register what happens when the S_test denominator lands below the gate that S_dev passed - currently that case has no branch. Optionally, equalize search budget across containers: GEPA gets 350 rollouts x 4 seeds to search the instruction space while the bank gets one distillation pass with k frozen at 7, so a high S may simply mean 'search beats no search'.
missing_baseline: The accuracy-matched, information-disjoint optimized instruction described above - an I1'(S_train2) trained on episodes disjoint from the bank's sources, evaluated in both xM0 and xM1 - which is the only arm that separates substitution from ceiling compression, and which the grid omits entirely. Two smaller omissions a reviewer will also press: (a) a search-budget-matched bank (bank curation, k, dedup threshold and item selection tuned on S_dev with the same rollout budget GEPA receives), since B and B_touched both leave the memory side unoptimized while the instruction side gets 1,400 rollouts; and (b) there is no I1xC or I1xM_all cell, so the paper's own recommendation - drop retrieval, serve one compiled instruction - is never measured in the configuration it recommends (optimized instruction plus compiled block). Prediction 3 is tested only at I0.
preprint_collision: The check is far above the median for form: dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), query and paper counts, by-id verification for 54 IDs, a named log file, an explicit withdrawal of v2's 'no published work uses one as the control for the other', and a residual-risk paragraph. It should be credited for that. But its evidentiary basis is weak in a way that matters here: arXiv is stated to be unreachable from the node and Semantic Scholar rate-limited, so every ID was confirmed through web-search snippets alone - a single channel, in direct tension with the proposal's own newly-enforced two-channel rule. The v2-to-v4 history is the tell: five citations were retracted as unverifiable and then all five reinstated, i.e. the verification procedure has already returned a wrong answer, and a procedure that produced false negatives can produce false positives. I cannot independently confirm EvoAgentBench (2607.05202), MemDelta (2606.29914), Experience Distillation (2607.21051), MemHarness (2607.28272) or the Skills paper (2608.14036), and the novelty case depends not just on EvoAgentBench existing but on a fine-grained negative claim about its table contents that snippet-level verification cannot support. Practical demand: report title, authors and abstract for at least the load-bearing IDs, and state which specific EvoAgentBench table was inspected. On coverage, I see no named collision that kills the proposal, but two search directions look under-covered: GEPA/DSPy-adjacent artifacts (repo issues, appendices of agent-framework and self-improving-agent systems papers, where 'optimizer plus memory' ablations characteristically live rather than in titles), and the skills/SKILL.md line, where 'compile a bank into a static procedure and compare against retrieval' is the natural ablation - 2608.14036 is cited only for the Workflow Memory comparison, and if its appendix already token-matches a compiled block against live retrieval, Prediction 3 and the C arm are pre-empted outright.
